sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Mr. Manoj Saxena - Advocate for the applicant.
Ms. Neelu Khetra Dy. GA for the respondent/State.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is second bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (now section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023) for grant of bail to the applicant, in connection with FIR/Crime No.533/2023, Date:-(Not mentioned) registered at P.S. - Rajgarh, District - Rajgarh(M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A, 304-B, 306, and 34 of the IPC.
2. Prosecution story, in brief is that marriage of the deceased Nirmalabai was solemnised on 12.05.2024 with the present applicant Chandan Prasad @ Sonu.
Co-accused Reshambai is mother-in-law of the deceased

, co-accused persons Anil@Chandra Prakash and Bhupendra @
Bhupesh are brother-in-law (Jeth) and Bharatsingh is father of the deceased.

It is alleged that 3-4 months later from the marriage when the deceased had NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:35311 2 MCRC-41707-2024 come to her maternal home, she told her parents that the present applicant and co-accused Reshambai are demanding a car in dowry
, her parents expressed that they are unable to fulfil the demand.
They had exhorted the deceased and sent back to her matrimonial home, but husband and mother- in-law did not stop and continued to demand of dowry and kept on physically and mentally harassing her.

Being severely bothered by the demand of dowry and the harassment on 10.06.2024 the deceased in her maternal home had committed Chandan Prasad @ Sonu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89034243/
1 suicide by hanging.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and has falsely been implicated in the case.
After dismissal of the first bail application of the applicant 09 prosecution witnesses have been examined before the trial court.

It is also submitted that however all the witnesses have supported the case of prosecution but there are material,
contradiction and omissions in their statements, therefore, their statements is not reliable.

It is also submitted that since before the marriage the deceased was suffering from illness and treatment was going on, therefore it cannot be said that the applicant has instigated the deceased to commit suicide.
It is also submitted that the application completed incarceration around 1 year and 5 months.
Trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

4. On other hand learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer by submitting that the applicant being husband of the deceased is the main accused of the incident there is clear allegation has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35311 3 MCRC-41707-2024 been levelled against him, bail petition of the co-accused Reshambai has been dismissed by this Court vide 31.06.024 in MCRC No.2179/2024, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

5. Having considered the submissions advanced from counsel for the parties, also perused the case diary and looking to the allegations levelled against the applicant, this Court is of the view that it is not a fit case to grant bail to the applicant.
Resultantly, M.Cr.C. is rejected.
(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE patil/a Chandan Prasad @ Sonu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89034243/
